relevance_rank_note: The original report of the ApoE4 Apoer2 recycling block and the only one of these three papers whose figures carry a directly tested ApoE3-vs-ApoE4 bracket; measures ApoE4 intracellular retention (B1 surrogate) and Apoer2 surface level (B2) in the same neurons, but does not measure ApoE-receptor binding itself.

description: Surface biotinylation of primary neurons after Reelin-stimulated receptor endocytosis: ApoE4 reduced surface Apoer2 to about half the ApoE3 level, and the ApoE3-vs-ApoE4 difference was tested directly with a bracket.
quote: ApoE3 was marginally, but not significantly, more effective than ApoE2, whereas ApoE4 led to a dramatic and statistically highly significant reduction of Apoer2 at the neuronal cell surface
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less surface Apoer2 under Reelin-stimulated endocytosis)
system: Mouse wildtype primary embryonic cortical neurons cultured 12-13 days; naturally secreted HDL-like human ApoE2, ApoE3 or ApoE4 lipoproteins 3 ug/mL with Reelin 2 ug/mL for 2 hr at 37 C; membrane-impermeable biotin surface labelling, neutravidin pulldown, surface/total Apoer2 immunoblot standardised to control
human_check: Bars read off an enlarged crop of Fig 1C: control+R 100, ApoE2+R ~60, ApoE3+R ~50, ApoE4+R ~25, so E4 is ~25 percentage points below E3. Please confirm; the source image is only 463x638 px so the reading is coarse. The P is from the ApoE3-to-ApoE4 bracket, which carries ** and the legend key '*P < 0.05; **P < 0.01; ***P < 0.001' plus 'Asterisks on brackets indicates significant difference between treatments' - this is a genuinely tested E3-vs-E4 contrast, unlike the control-only brackets in the two eLife papers. n is N/A because the stated 'four independent experiments' appears in the panel B legend and panel C says only that it was quantitated as described in B.

description: Surface biotinylation without Reelin stimulation: ApoE4 lowered surface Apoer2 while ApoE2 and ApoE3 did not reduce it relative to control, with a tested ApoE3-vs-ApoE4 difference.
quote: Whereas ApoE2 (lane 2) and ApoE3 (lane 3) did not reduce surface expression of Apoer2 compared with the control (lane 1), ApoE4 significantly decreased surface expression of this
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less surface Apoer2 at baseline, without Reelin)
system: Mouse wildtype primary embryonic cortical neurons cultured 12-13 days; naturally secreted HDL-like human ApoE2, ApoE3 or ApoE4 lipoproteins 3 ug/mL for 15 min at 37 C, no Reelin; membrane-impermeable biotin surface labelling, neutravidin pulldown, surface/total Apoer2 immunoblot standardised to control
human_check: Bars read off an enlarged crop of Fig 1B: control 100, ApoE2 ~114, ApoE3 ~83, ApoE4 ~64, so E4 is ~19 percentage points below E3. Please confirm. The P is from the ApoE3-to-ApoE4 bracket carrying a single * against the panel B key '*P < 0.05; **P < 0.01'; a second bracket (ApoE2 vs ApoE4) carries ** and must not be read onto this row. n=4 from 'four independent experiments' in the panel B legend.

description: Pulse-chase of secreted ApoE in primary neurons after a suramin wash removed surface-bound ApoE: ApoE4 was released into the medium more slowly and more of it stayed inside the cell at every chase time, showing ApoE4 itself is retained intracellularly rather than retroendocytosed.
quote: Substantially more ApoE4 was retained in intracellular compartments at all time points, confirming that impaired recycling of ApoE4 also occurs in primary neurons
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more ApoE retained intracellularly, slower release to medium)
system: Mouse wildtype primary embryonic cortical neurons cultured 12-13 days; naturally secreted human ApoE2, ApoE3 or ApoE4 lipoproteins 3 ug/mL 15-30 min at 37 C, suramin wash to strip surface-bound ApoE, chase 30 min, 1 hr or 2 hr; ApoE immunoprecipitated from chase medium and lysate, immunoblot
human_check: Fig 1A is a representative immunoblot with no bar graph, no quantification, no stars and no stated n, so effect is qualitative and P and n are absent. This is ApoE4 retention on its own, not ApoE measured together with the receptor, so it is a class 3 surrogate of B1 rather than a binding measurement; the link to Apoer2 retention is the authors' inference across panels A and B.
